wtt.form: WTP = -ln(u) x VoT / beta, beta = clip(beta0 x VoT_ref / VoT, beta_clip), u ~ U(0,1) once per commuter (Layer A); a CAR option whose charge is above WTP is not offered; company cars and commuters with neither PT nor WFH are exempt
wtt.status: beta0 searched; beta_clip [SSC] and vot_ref [A] fixed, not searched

fuel.status: fixed input (config.toml: author-supplied petrol price, Oct 2026, x 9.0 L/100 km); not searched
fuel.form: car fuel = round(2 x path_km x fuel_cost_per_km, 2); 0 for company cars; v3_relative WFH carries it like parking

base_car.what: car share, mean of days 6-10 (pre-charge), R-daily

change_21_30.what: car cordon crossings, mean days 21-30 vs mean days 6-10

change_11_13.what: overshoot, mean days 11-13 vs days 6-10 (may reach about -30%)

structural_fixes.from: all_days (EMA of the fee PAID, 0 on non-car days)
structural_fixes.to: faced (EMA, alpha = memory.ema_alpha, of the fee FACED at the car reference departure on every day)
structural_fixes.why: [v3 5.2 fee-ref, with two differences [A]: on car days the fee actually paid (after retiming) rather than the fee at h0, and alpha 0.3 (SPEC) rather than 0.2]. With the paid fee, agents who left the car kept a reference of 0 and a loss term on the full fee for ever, so the day-11 response could not fade.
[v3 4.4 capped variant; De Borger and Fosgerau 2008: a total weight of 4 is generous]. The loss term was larger than the fee itself for day-11 leavers.

structural_fixes.from: spec (WFH = k_WFH x phi; saves car time and parking)
structural_fixes.to: v3_relative (WFH = k_WFH x phi + VoT/60 x free-flow time + parking + fuel)
structural_fixes.why: [v3 6.2: WFH has no PARK term; zero-fee property]. WFH no longer earns the commute, parking and fuel as savings; it still avoids congestion delay, schedule delay and the charge.

structural_fixes.from: 0 (no fuel cost; v3 folded fuel into its parking value)
structural_fixes.to: 0.30 NZ$/km, fixed input (petrol NZ$3.30/L [author-supplied, Oct 2026] x 9.0 L/100 km); car fuel = 2 x path_km x 0.30, 0 for company cars
structural_fixes.why: Driving cost only time, schedule delay, charge and parking, so a calibrated parking value also stood for fuel. Fuel is explicit and is not a calibration scalar.

structural_fixes.from: [8, 8, 8, 0, 6] [v3], then searched (17 without fuel, 11 with fuel 0.23)
structural_fixes.to: [17, 17, 17, 0, 12.75], fixed input [author decision; consistent with the AT 2014 Victoria St daily rate]
structural_fixes.why: Paid parking is set from real-world knowledge and is no longer a calibration scalar.
[A, Verplanken et al. 2008]: habit discontinuity is a change of the performance context; a price change leaves route, time and cues intact, so kappa_H is no longer halved at the charge wake.

[v3 6.2 PAP NZ$8, swept {4, 8, 12}, in v3's form omega(P) x PAP x HTA/2]; free scalar 1 of 3 (the others are k_WFH, searched in 2-16, and wtt.beta0), entered in the specification form omega(P) x (VoT/60 x T_pt + PAP), so the value is not comparable with v3's.

structural_fixes.from: SKIP (postpone or cancel the day) at NZ$25, later NZ$30, plus one hour of VoT
structural_fixes.to: removed: every commuter chooses among CAR (a departure time), PT and WFH where allowed
structural_fixes.why: [author decision 2026-10-09] SKIP had become a permanent choice rather than a one-day postponement (at a NZ$30 peak 97 of R-clock's 102 skippers skipped all of days 21-30; at NZ$6, 8 commuters skipped every day), and in the rule arms every skipper could have taken PT. The SKIP-share target goes with it.

structural_fixes.to: WTP = -ln(u) x VoT / beta, beta = clip(beta0 x VoT_ref / VoT, 0.1, 2.0), u ~ U(0,1) fixed per commuter; a CAR option charged above WTP is not offered; beta0 searched (free scalar 3 of 3)
structural_fixes.why: [author decision 2026-10-09; SSC2026 akl_pricing.nls exponential decay, base_beta 0.5] The share willing to pay a charge F falls as exp(-beta F / VoT). Company cars and commuters with neither PT nor WFH are exempt. It applies in every arm as a choice-set constraint, and not on uncharged days.

structural_fixes.from: seed-1 scale used for every seed
structural_fixes.to: recalibrated per seed and per evaluated (PAP, k_WFH) pair; data/calibration.json holds by_seed records
structural_fixes.why: Pre-charge congestion feeds back on the response. The calibration has no charge, so it does not depend on beta0.

capacity_procedure: nested: for every (PAP, k_WFH) pair and seed, cordonlite.run.calibrate (default bracket and tolerance) is run with that pair's behaviour parameters, then the 30-day charged runs of every beta0 of the pair use the resulting scale (the calibration has no charge, so the willingness to pay removes nothing and the scale does not depend on beta0); it targets the car-weighted peak 15-min queue + road delay (engine.calib_delay = 'total') of 15 min

road.status: fixed inputs (config.toml [road], k from data/road_meta.json); not searched

search.method: staged grid over PAP x k_WFH x beta0 (paid parking fixed at NZ$17); capacity calibrated once per (PAP, k_WFH, seed) and shared by every beta0 of that pair (the calibration has no charge, so the willingness to pay removes nothing and the scale does not depend on beta0). Stage 1: beta0 in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} on PAP 21-23 x k_WFH {4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 16} around the two-scalar optimum (PAP 22, k_WFH 9) and on the four corners of the NZ$1 grid (PAP 10 and 36 x k_WFH 2 and 16). Stage 2: the full NZ$1 k_WFH range 2-16 at every stage-1 beta0, on each PAP of stage 1 at which some k_WFH meets the three base-share targets (the base shares do not depend on beta0), plus the next PAP outwards when such a PAP is at the edge of 21-23. Stage 3: one finer beta0 step, the midpoints between the beta0 the rule chooses after stage 2 and its neighbours in the stage-1 list, on the stage-2 pairs. beta0 = 0 (no limit) is run on every stage 1-2 pair as a reference and never selected. Seeds 1-3; selection over every non-reference point of the three stages.
search.selection: lexicographic: (1) feasible = every 3-seed mean in its target band at the targets' stated precision (shares to 2 decimals, changes to whole percent) and every seed within the stated single-seed tolerance; (2) among feasible points, the smallest squared relative distance to the anchors (PAP 8 [v3], paid parking 17 [AT car-park all-day rate 2014], k_WFH 8 [v3], beta0 0.5 [SSC2026 base_beta]); (3) loss as tie-break. If no point is feasible, the lowest loss. Points with beta0 = 0 (no willingness-to-pay limit) are references and are never selected.
search.loss_doc: Loss of one grid point over its seeds. centre: sum of squared (3-seed mean - centre) / scale for base car, base PT and the d21-30 response (scales 0.05, 0.035, 0.04); band: squared band excess of the 3-seed means for every target (scale 0.02), plus squared excess beyond the stated single-seed tolerance for each seed; prior: 0.02 x sum of squared relative distances of the scalars from the design values (PAP, parking and k_WFH 8 [v3]; beta0 0.5 [SSC2026 base_beta]), a weak tie-break toward them.

Each variant changes one of the fixed assumptions (the willingness-to-pay form, early-start option) or sets beta0 to 0 or 0.5 at the chosen PAP, k_WFH and (otherwise) beta0 (no new search), on seeds 1-3 with nested capacity calibration, to show how much the result depends on it.

variants.label: early6

gap_sensitivity.reading: The willingness to travel and the early start do different jobs. Without the willingness to travel (beta0 = 0) the chosen PAP and k_WFH give -14.5% on days 21-30 (overshoot -18.7%), inside the band but well short of its centre, and no commuter loses the car; with SSC2026's beta0 0.5 the response is -32.3% (overshoot -35.5%) and 21.9% of commuters have no car option, beyond the band on every seed. Taking VoT_ref from the simulated commuters' median VoT instead of exp(vot_mu) leaves the response practically unchanged (-21.4%). The early start keeps the chosen point feasible: without it the response is -22.8% and seed 2 reaches -24.3%, beyond the tolerance, and the 08:00 to 09:00 crossings fall by 38.7% against 42.2% with it. How much the early start is used depends on its assumed cost: at NZ$1.5 x phi(F) 14.0% of commuters start early before the charge and 17.0% after it, and the peak crossings fall by 46.3%; at NZ$6 x phi(F) the option is almost unused (0.018, then 0.014). Giving the permission to every employee of the three eligible groups raises the share to 0.102 before and 0.124 after the charge. These three variants raise base car to 0.856-0.858, above the band at the stated precision (and at NZ$6 x phi(F) seed 2 responds by -24.6%, beyond the tolerance). None of the variants was searched or adopted; 'feasible' is judged at the chosen PAP, k_WFH and beta0 only.

out_of_sample.note: Out-of-sample checks run after the selection; they did not influence it. Capacity is recalibrated per seed as in the search.

limits: The targets are stated assumptions, and the response anchors are not like-for-like: Stockholm and Gothenburg measured total cordon traffic in charged hours over months to years, while the band here applies to AM car commuters over days 21-30. v3 10.5 asks for a qualitative comparison only; the private-car commuter response is likely larger than the total-traffic one.

Behaviour is calibrated at the NZ$6 peak of the SSC2026 schedule only. Runs at other peaks (fees.peak_fee 0, 3, 12, 18, 30) extrapolate the fitted model, and the willingness to travel makes the extrapolation steep by construction: the share willing to pay falls as exp(-beta F / VoT), so a higher peak removes the car for more commuters whatever the rest of the cost model says.

15 of 489 points are feasible, all at PAP 22, on a ridge in k_WFH and beta0: k_WFH 10 with beta0 0.05, 11 with 0.05-0.1, 12 with 0.05-0.15, 13 with 0.05-0.2 and 14 with 0.05-0.25. At the stated precision base PT is 0.16 at PAP 21 for every k_WFH; base car is 0.86 or more at PAP 22 from k_WFH 15, at PAP 23 from k_WFH 7 and at PAP 24 from k_WFH 6, and the lower k_WFH that keep the base shares in band at PAP 23-24 respond by -27.7% or more on days 21-30 even without the willingness to travel. The rule picks PAP 22 / k_WFH 12 / beta0 0.15, the feasible point nearest the anchors. The next ones are k_WFH 13 / beta0 0.2 (anchor distance 3.813 against 3.802), k_WFH 11 / beta0 0.1 (3.843) and k_WFH 14 / beta0 0.25 (3.875): the targets fix the ridge and the anchors choose the point on it. The lowest-loss point is k_WFH 10 / beta0 0.05 (loss 2.03 against 2.18). On unrounded 3-seed means no point is feasible, because base car is 0.853-0.855 at every feasible point. On the calibration seeds base car is above 0.85 on seeds 1 and 2 (0.853, 0.859) and the days 21-30 response is beyond -22% on seed 2 (-23.1%), all within the stated tolerance. The targets were not relaxed.

The response is close to the centre of the band: -21.4% on seeds 1-3 (-20.9%, -23.1%, -20.4%), -21.1% on unseen seeds 6-12 (single seeds -19.2% to -23.1%) and -21.3% over seeds 1-12, with an overshoot of -25.2%, -25.4% and -25.3%. Base car runs high out of sample: 0.863 on the unseen seeds 6-12 and 0.859 over seeds 1-12, both above the band at the stated precision. It is above 0.85 on held-out seed 4 and on every unseen seed except 11 (0.859 to 0.875), all within the tolerance; base PT is 0.136 and 0.140, above 0.15 only on seeds 5 and 11 (0.153, 0.151). The chosen point sits at the top of the base car band because base car rises as k_WFH removes the last WFH days (0.849 at k_WFH 9, 0.854 at 12), and the 0.2% who skipped before the charge now choose among car, PT and WFH.

The willingness to travel does much of the work. At the chosen point 14.2% of commuters have a WTP below the NZ$6 peak (exempt company cars and trades included); on charged days 8.3% have no car option left, the same share on days 11-13 and 21-30 because the threshold is fixed, 11.6% have at least one car option removed, and 5.6% of all commuters are left with PT only (decider 'forced'). Without it (beta0 = 0, same PAP and k_WFH) the days 21-30 response is -14.5% and the overshoot -18.7%; with SSC2026's beta0 0.5 they are -32.3% and -35.5%, and 21.9% of commuters have no car option. Because beta is clipped below at 0.1, any positive beta0 removes some car options: beta0 0.05 already leaves 4.3% of commuters without a car and strengthens the response by 3.7 pp (-14.5% to -18.2% at k_WFH 12). The limit cannot be made weaker than that floor except by switching it off. VoT_ref from the simulated commuters' median VoT instead of exp(vot_mu) leaves the response practically unchanged (-21.4%).

With the charge more commuters start early. About 48% may start early; 7.6% of all commuters do so on days 6-10 (8.8% of car users), 9.4% on days 11-13 and 9.5% on days 21-30, against 6.9% in the no-charge run; as a share of the fewer remaining car users it is 14.1%. The money saved by crossing early (NZ$4 before 07:30 against NZ$6 from 08:00 to 09:00, plus the loss term, and for some commuters the only charge they are willing to pay) is weighed against the assumed inconvenience of NZ$3 x phi(F), and the result depends on that assumed cost: at NZ$1.5 x phi(F) the share is 14.0% before and 17.0% after the charge and the 08:00 to 09:00 crossings fall by 46.3%; at NZ$6 x phi(F) almost nobody starts early (0.018, then 0.014). Without the early start the days 21-30 response is -22.8% and seed 2 reaches -24.3%, beyond the tolerance. The cost and the permission probabilities are assumptions with no empirical source.

Peak spreading is clear in every seed. Car crossings in the 08:00 to 09:00 peak (NZ$6) fall by 42.2% from days 6-10 to days 21-30 against 21.4% over the whole morning (seeds 1-3: 44.1%, 39.9%, 42.5% against 20.9%, 23.1%, 20.4%), and by 43.4% on unseen seeds 6-12 (43.0% over seeds 1-12). Crossings before 07:30 rise by 14.0% on seeds 1-3 (+18.4%, +5.2%, +18.3%) and by 13.5% over seeds 1-12. Against the no-charge run the 08:00 to 09:00 share of crossings falls in every seed (-0.129, -0.098, -0.132) and the 07:00 to 08:00 share rises (+0.065, +0.051, +0.081). In the paired check 32.8% of commuters who drive in both runs have a different modal departure with the charge, 20.9% earlier and 11.8% later (mean shift -9.8 minutes).

Day-to-day churn in the daily rule arm is large: 25% of commuters have a different modal car departure on days 26-30 than on days 6-10 with the charge, and 23% without it. A before-and-after count of retimers therefore says little, and retiming is reported against the no-charge run.

PAP is a fitted residual. With parking and fuel fixed, PAP is the only scalar that can hold the assumed pre-charge split, and the willingness to travel does not move that split; it is 22 again (v3 PAP 22-44 in v3's form, against v3's NZ$8 swept 4-12). At PAP 22 commuters with P = 1-2 practically never ride PT before the charge (PT share 0.002 and 0.003 in the population manipulation); after it 5.6% and 5.8% do (+0.055 and +0.058 against the no-charge run; 0.000 in the two-scalar search without the willingness to travel). The baseline shares react sharply to PAP (at k_WFH 12: base PT 0.160, 0.145, 0.128 and 0.116 at PAP 21-24), the response much less (-21.4%, -20.9% and -20.0% at PAP 22-24 with beta0 0.15).

k_WFH and beta0 are identified together, by the response and the overshoot, not by the WFH share (base WFH 0.001 at k_WFH 12). At PAP 22 and beta0 0.15 the days 21-30 response is -24.3%, -22.4%, -21.4%, -20.0% and -19.4% at k_WFH 10-14 (overshoot -28.5% to -23.1%); at k_WFH 12 it is -14.5%, -18.2%, -19.5%, -21.4%, -22.9%, -24.2%, -26.4% and -32.3% at beta0 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3 and 0.5. Along the ridge one NZ$ of k_WFH offsets about 0.05 of beta0. A realistic hybrid-work baseline is not reproduced: k_WFH 4 gives 7.4% WFH before the charge but a response of -36.5% at beta0 0.15. With k_WFH 12 WFH is a small margin (0.1% before the charge, 4.2% on days 21-30). v3's WFH quota (1-3 days per 5-day block) would bound it; it is not implemented.

The fixed inputs carry their own uncertainty. The petrol price (NZ$3.30/L) is author-supplied for October 2026 and was not verified here; the last published figure we read was NZ$2.97/L for September 2026. Consumption is 9.0 L/100 km for every paying driver; electric vehicles, fuel cards and other running costs are not represented. Paid parking NZ$17 is a 2014 casual all-day rate, applied to half of office commuters (the other half park free). The early start time (07:00), its cost (NZ$3 x phi(F)) and the permission probabilities (0.8, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0) are author assumptions, and so is the form of the willingness to travel: a threshold fixed per commuter (SSC2026 draws entry every day), beta clipped to 0.1-2.0, VoT_ref the median of the VoT distribution, no base trip rate and no 0.05-0.95 clip. Base years are mixed (2026 fuel, 2025 fare and charge, 2014 parking). The road layer is fixed as well and is not searched: section capacity k = 0.076999 x directional ADT, BPR alpha 0.15 and beta 4 with a speed floor of 0.18, and the motorway breakdown rule (breakdown at V/C 1.0, recovery below 0.95, discharge capacity 10% lower, speed at most 0.45 of free flow).

The design-valued model (PAP 8, k_WFH 8, beta0 0.5) with the fixed parking and fuel has base car 0.556 and PT 0.441, far outside the baseline bands, and responds by -40.0% (overshoot -45.2%). Without fuel, with v3's NZ$8 parking and without the willingness to travel (300 agents, free-flow roads) the v3-valued model gave -15.4% (overshoot -25.0%). The scalars were moved to meet the assumed baseline.

The choice does not depend on the soft overshoot bound (the same 15 points are feasible, and the same point is chosen, for bounds of -30% to -33%), but where it lies on the ridge depends on the anchors (see above). No other point becomes feasible with the relaxed bound, so the two ridge alternatives checked out of sample are the points nearest the anchors among the ten lowest-loss other points, PAP 22 / k_WFH 11 / beta0 0.1 and PAP 22 / k_WFH 10 / beta0 0.05. On seeds 4-12 they give -20.7% and -21.0% (base car 0.860 and 0.858), against -21.2% (base car 0.861) for the chosen point: out of sample the ridge points are hard to tell apart.

Capacity is a further calibrated quantity, recalibrated per (PAP, k_WFH) pair and seed against the peak queue + road delay; it does not depend on beta0. Its discrete steps add noise to the base shares: at the chosen point the scale is 0.4303 on seed 1 and 0.3961 on seeds 2-3 (0.3961 on all three at k_WFH 9), and 0.3646 to 0.4303 on seeds 4-12. The gate queue is the smaller part of the 15-minute target: at the chosen point (seeds 1-3, days 6-10) the car-weighted peak 15-min queue + road delay is 14.9 minutes, the peak of the queue delay alone 4.6 minutes and the mean road delay of a car 7.3 minutes. On days 21-30 the charge brings the peak queue delay down to 1.2 minutes, the peak queue + road delay to 9.8 minutes and the mean road delay to 5.9 minutes.

Single-agent example (tests/test_rules.py; no willingness-to-pay limit in the example): for the shared Layer A with paid parking NZ$17 and the fuel cost of a 20 km path, 250 of the 625 trait combinations ride PT before the charge. Of the other 375, without the early-start permission 317 keep the car at the usual time on the charge morning, 54 switch to PT and 4 retime by 15 minutes (H = 1); the two that postponed the day until SKIP was removed now keep driving. With the permission 300 keep, 53 switch to PT and 22 leave at 06:30 for the 07:00 start. The v3 worked example (identical A: pay / PT / retime) still separates only with the v3 settings or with free parking.

H damps the charge wake only at levels 4-5 (days 11-13: -26.5%, -27.4%, -27.0% at H = 1-3, -25.2% and -23.0% at H = 4-5), and not in the long run (-20.0% to -21.6%): habit re-forms on the new mode immediately.

The charge-induced switch to PT is largest at P = 3 (+0.197 against the no-charge run; +0.156 and +0.142 at P = 4-5, +0.055 and +0.058 at P = 1-2): at P = 4-5 many PT-feasible agents already ride PT without the charge (0.40 and 0.58 of them at days 26-30 in the no-charge run, who-adapts tables). The PT share after the charge rises with P (0.06, 0.06, 0.27, 0.50, 0.60).

The F response gradient (-17.8% at F = 1 to -33.9% at F = 5) still comes mainly from daily WFH of F = 4-5 hybrid workers (no quota; WFH share 0.17 at F = 5 on days 21-30 with the charge). The 08:00 to 09:00 share of crossings falls with F against the no-charge run (+0.010 at F = 1 to -0.218 at F = 5), partly because phi(F) scales the cost of the early day, and retiming of car keepers against the no-charge run is larger at F = 3-5 (+0.120, +0.158, +0.133) than at F = 1-2 (-0.010, +0.066).
Who-adapts tables conditional on being a day-10 driver are biased by selection; the population manipulation is the unbiased check.

The reference fee follows the fee faced, but on car days it uses the fee actually paid (after retiming; v3 uses the fee at h0 before retiming) and alpha 0.3 (SPEC; v3 0.2), so a retimer keeps a loss term on returning to the peak.

The start an option is measured against is chosen from the expected arrival on the morning of the decision and is kept for the outcome: a commuter who planned the 07:00 start and is held up counts as late for 07:00 (and can be woken by T3), not as early for the usual start. For an agent on a standing plan the start is re-read from that morning's expected arrival.

Only the R-daily arm is calibrated, and the clock arms are not run for this report. The LLM deciders are not calibrated, but the shared Layer A inputs (parking, fuel, the early-start permission and the willingness to pay, which removes the same car options in every arm) reach the LLM arms. The rule's WFH earns no parking, fuel or commute credit while the prompt states both daily costs, so live-LLM WFH shares are not comparable with the rule arm on this margin, and a live LLM is not told the rule's NZ$3 x phi(F) cost of the early day (it reads the flexibility sentence instead). MockLLM re-weights the same GC parts; its response at the chosen values is not measured here.
